description: Change of use from Salvation Army Hall (Class F2) to Buddhist Community Centre London Branch (Class F1(f)) with ancillary residential accommodation and associated internal alterations.
decision_conditions: The application submission fails to fully demonstrate that the proposal would not give rise to adverse impacts upon the highway network to the detriment of traffic congestion, parking stress and highway safety. Based on the limited information submitted, the proposed development is considered to have an unacceptable impact on highway safety. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DME 4 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), and Policies T2, T4 and T5 of the London Plan (2021), and is refused in accordance with paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

In the absence of a Air Quality Assessment and Transport Assessment no evidence regarding the potential trip generation has been provided. Given the uncertainty in the levels of trip generation associated with the proposed change of use, it is not possible to ascertain the full measure of transport emissions and whether the proposed development would be air quality neutral. Further, the proposed development is not air quality positive and no measures are proposed to mitigate net increases in emissions. It is therefore considered that the proposed development would contribute to the production of unacceptable pollutant emissions in the Uxbridge Road Air Quality Focus Area, contrary to Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), Policy DMEI 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policy SI 1 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Given its proposed usage, internal layout, inclusion of residential accommodation and lack of information regarding noise impacts, it is considered that the proposed development would result in a significant increase in activity (people and vehicle movements), undue noise and general disturbance to neighbouring residents, subsequently harming their living conditions and amenities. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the requirements of Policies DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020) and paragraph 135 (f) of the NPPF (2024).

Insufficient information has been submitted to justify the provision of the proposed use or loss of the existing use, the proposed development is therefore contrary to Policies DMCI 1 and DMCI 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), as well as Policy S1 (C) of the London Plan (2021).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
